questions.q: What is a SYNONYM in SQL Server?
options: A type of trigger that fires on INSERT
An alias for another database object, which you can query as if it were the real thing
A backup copy of a table's data
A constraint that enforces uniqueness
questions.explain: CREATE SYNONYM defines a short, stable name that points at another object, queried exactly like the original.

questions.q: Can a synonym point to an object on a different server?
options: No, synonyms can only reference views, never tables
Yes, but only for stored procedures, not tables
Yes, via a linked server, in addition to the same or a different database
No, synonyms can only reference objects in the same database
questions.explain: A synonym can reference an object in the same database, a different database on the same server, or a different server via a linked server.

questions.q: What real problem does a synonym solve when the underlying object is renamed or migrated?
options: Code can keep referencing the stable synonym name, needing only the synonym's definition updated once
It automatically updates every query in the database
It makes the underlying object impossible to drop
It prevents the underlying object from ever being renamed
questions.explain: Without a synonym, every reference to the old name would need to be found and rewritten; with one, you update the synonym's target in one place.

questions.q: After 'CREATE SYNONYM dbo.Products FOR AdventureWorks2012.Production.Product;', how do you query it?
options: Synonyms cannot be queried with SELECT at all
You must still use the full original name; the synonym is read-only reference documentation
SELECT * FROM dbo.Products — exactly as if it were the real table
SELECT * FROM SYNONYM dbo.Products
questions.explain: Once created, a synonym behaves exactly like the object it points to for querying purposes.

questions.q: Why might a reporting database create a synonym for a table in a different database?
options: To automatically copy the table's data into the reporting database
To give code a short, local, stable name instead of repeating a long cross-database reference everywhere
Because synonyms are required before any cross-database query is allowed
Because the original table cannot be queried directly from another database under any circumstances
questions.explain: A synonym simplifies references to simplify code, not because the longer name would be otherwise unusable.
